messages.author: 1e1f02e079119aa4
messages.subject: Models without intercept
parts:
I'm using pcount for abundance estimation at 5 national parks, each of
which have around 25 sampling locations. I'd like to use "park" as a
group effect (i.e., 5 columns, one for each park, with 1s and 0s for
whether each sampling location occurs in a given park). The idea is
that this will essentially function as a different model intercept for
each park.

Since I'm explicitly including these group effect terms, I'd like to
run the pcount models without a model intercept, but haven't found a
way to do this.

Any advice on ways to run a pcount model without an intercept?

Thanks!

messages.author: 6a288128bce8283d
messages.subject: Re: Models without intercept
parts:
That's fairly straight forward:

If you take the example from the pcount function documentation accessed via:

?pcount

the code in there produces a no intercept model:

# Fit a model
fm1 <- pcount(~visit - 1 ~ x, umf, K=50)

the "-1" in the function call indicates that you don't want an intercept.

Cheers,
Richard S

messages.author: 527e14923215b7e4
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: Models without intercept
parts:
Richard is right that "~-1" will remove the intercept. Also, you don't need to create the dummy variables because they are created automatically when you provide a factor in a formula. So, if you have a single column for "park", which contains the name of each park, then you can use:

pcount(~1 ~park-1, umf)

Richard
